chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to cover “new events only; old events untouched,” but it never exercises the actual upgrade path where an existing log is opened and then appended to with the lowered threshold. It only generates an old log, reads it twice, and asserts the `.jsonl` bytes are unchanged. A regression that rewrites or backfills old inline evidence when the first new event is appended after upgrade would pass this suite: `test_an_old_log_replays_identically_and_is_not_rewritten` performs no append, `test_new_events_are_at_least_30_percent_smaller` uses fresh logs, and the master-switch test also uses a fresh log. For example, if `EventLog.append` on an existing project with `evidence_blobs=True` compacts the shard and externalizes old gate evidence, the old bytes change in violation of the stated upgrade-safety promise, but no test here catches it [r-upgrade-safe, r-replay-compat].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_evidence_inline_threshold.py:test_an_old_log_replays_identically_and_is_not_rewritten

chunk_findings.detail: The lowered threshold is inert in the default configuration because `log.evidence_blobs` is still off by default (the upgrade note says the master switch stays off, and the new tests include `test_master_switch_default_is_unchanged`). Given a default project and a new `gate.passed`/`gate.failed` event containing, say, a 512-byte `command_output_tail` or reviewer finding, the evidence remains inline before and after this patch; no blob is written and the serialized event size is unchanged. Thus the stated goal/falsifier (“new gate event bytes at least 30 percent lower”) is not achieved by this change alone—it requires separately enabling `log.evidence_blobs` [R-scalability].

chunk_findings.detail: The change lowers the default of the existing `log.evidence_blob_min_bytes` knob from `1024` to `256`, but the stated conformance requires the new behaviour to be behind a new knob that defaults to the old behaviour [r-upgrade-safe]. Concretely, a project that already has `log.evidence_blobs = true` but has not set `log.evidence_blob_min_bytes` will silently change behaviour after upgrade: a 300-byte command-output tail that previously stayed inline in the gate event will now be written as a blob reference. That is not an opt-in change, and the knob’s own documentation warns that readers not taught to read blobs back see a reference where they expect the value.

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims old logs “replay identically,” but it only compares `first.items.keys()` and the per-item `gates` mappings. If `fold(..., strict=False)` returns an empty model because a regression or malformed event handling silently skips events, both `first` and `again` are empty and the assertions pass even though no replay occurred. Likewise, a regression that changes non-gate fields (title, status, other task state) while leaving `gates` equal would also pass. This does not actually enforce the promised [r-replay-compat] / [r-upgrade-safe] behaviour.

chunk_findings.detail: The test only checks that the first `len(old_lines)` lines of the shard chosen by `next(events.glob("*.jsonl"))` are unchanged. It never asserts that the new `gate.passed` event was appended after those old lines in that same shard. If `EventLog` rotates to a different shard, or if `logfixture` produces multiple shards and `glob` selects a non-head shard, the old lines remain byte-identical and `fold` can still see `TNEW`, so the test passes even though the docstring’s “gains a small-stub event at the tail” promise is false. This weakens the [r-upgrade-safe] test coverage.

chunk_findings.detail: The new tail assertion assumes the `shard` path chosen by `next(events.glob("*.jsonl"))` before the appends is the same shard `EventLog.append` will write to. `Path.glob` iteration order is unspecified and the fixture can produce multiple rotated `.jsonl` shards. If `glob` returns a non-head shard, the new `gate.passed` event lands in the head shard, so `now[-1]` is an old line that does not contain `"TNEW"`, and the assertion fails even though append/rotation behavior is correct. This makes the regression test flaky in the multi-shard case.
